#schema: # The entry points a coordinator may dispatch a worker into, read by
# skills/coordinate/scripts/dispatch-common.sh. Seven tab-separated fields:
#   1 skill     the shirabe skill the worker runs, as /shirabe:<skill>
#   2 leg       the koto request leg the skill answers with --koto-leg, or -
#               when the skill doesn't accept --koto-leg. A skill answers only
#               its own leg name, so this is fixed per skill.
#   3 template  the template file names a leg admits on attach, comma-joined,
#               or - with no leg
#   4 pinned    the leg inputs to pin, as VAR=source pairs comma-joined, or -.
#               Sources: `arg` (the positional argument) and `plan-slug` (the
#               positional PLAN path's slug, PLAN-<slug>.md).
#   5 flags     the flags a brief may give the skill, comma-joined, or -. A
#               trailing `=*` admits any value after the `=`. --koto-leg is in
#               no row: the dispatch script adds it. --upstream is in no row:
#               it takes a separate value token the allow-list can't vet.
#   6 visibility the visibility every repository the unit lands in must have:
#               `any`, `public` or `private`. render-brief.sh reads each
#               target's visibility live from GitHub and refuses a dispatch
#               whose target this entry point can't take, before any leg is
#               opened or holding written. A unit's targets are the brief
#               input's `repo` and its `targets` (for a PLAN-driven unit, the
#               repositories its issues land in).
#   7 instead    the entry point to name in that refusal, the one that takes
#               the target (with its own positional and flags), or - when
#               there is none
# No entry point restricts its targets' visibility today: /deliver and
# /execute ran only in public repositories until shirabe#505, and the column is
# kept for the next requirement an entry point adds.
# /deliver and /work-on answer legs since shirabe#407. /work-on answers its
# leg only for an issue or a task, never for a PLAN path, so dispatch-worker.sh
# opens no leg for a /work-on worker whose argument is one.
scope
